literal: Without leaving, him who went, with eyes to see, do not set, may you live, moon.
translation: O moon, may you live long! Do not set, so that I may see with my own eyes him who departed without ever leaving my heart.
modern: நிலவே, நீ நீடூழி வாழ்வாயாக! என் நெஞ்சை விட்டு அகலாமல் பிரிந்து சென்ற என் காதலரை நான் என் கண்களால் காணும் பொருட்டு நீ மறையாமல் இருப்பாயாக.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks directly to the moon (மதி), wishing it a long life (வாழி) as she begs it not to set (படாஅதி). She relies on the moonlight to search for her lover, who has physically journeyed away (சென்றாரை) yet remains constantly in her thoughts without leaving (விடாஅது). The poetic elongation of sounds (alapeṭai) in the words for 'without leaving' and 'do not set' beautifully mirrors her drawn-out yearning and her desire to stretch the night.
